headline: FAA nationwide ground stop after telecommunications failure, lifted the same evening
fact: On November 13, 2026, at about 3:30 p.m. Eastern Time, the FAA issued a nationwide ground stop after a telecommunications problem destabilized communications and radar feeds at 17 of 22 Air Route Traffic Control Centers. The agency said the system was stabilized and air traffic resumed at 8:15 p.m. the same day.
source: Federal Aviation Administration, Nationwide Ground Stop: Questions and Answers

headline: FAA reports about 12,462 cancellations on the ground-stop day, with recovery still underway on November 15
fact: The FAA's November 15 Q&A says operators canceled about 12,462 flights on Friday, November 13, including 9,082 cancellations by major airlines, and notes that not all of those cancellations were caused directly by the ground stop. About 3,500 aircraft already airborne landed safely. The agency said the system was stable and that recovery to normal operations would be slow and steady.
source: Federal Aviation Administration, Nationwide Ground Stop: Questions and Answers

headline: FAA extends Newark scheduled-operations cap through October 30, 2027
fact: A Federal Register extension published June 23, 2026, keeps scheduled operations at Newark Liberty International Airport limited to 36 arrivals and 36 departures per hour (72 hourly operations) from 6:00 a.m. through 10:59 p.m. Eastern Time. The action is effective October 25, 2026, and expires October 30, 2027. The FAA cites continued air-traffic-controller staffing shortfalls at Philadelphia TRACON Area C, which handles Newark arrivals and departures.
source: Federal Register, Operating Limitations at Newark Liberty International Airport (2026-12589)

headline: 2025 shutdown emergency order cut flights at 40 high-traffic airports; no 2026 successor order found
fact: On November 6, 2025, DOT and the FAA announced a temporary reduction of scheduled domestic operations at 40 high-traffic airports, beginning at 4 percent on November 7, 2025, and stepping up toward 10 percent by November 14, 2025, because of air-traffic-controller staffing strain during a lapse in appropriations. A search of FAA and DOT newsroom pages found no comparable 2026 government-shutdown flight-cut emergency order still in effect as of mid-November 2026.
source: Federal Aviation Administration, DOT and FAA Announce Temporary 10% Reduction in Flights at 40 Airports

headline: FAA terminated the 2025 flight-reduction emergency order on November 17, 2025
fact: DOT and the FAA announced that the flight-reduction emergency order would end at 6:00 a.m. on Monday, November 17, 2025, returning the National Airspace System to normal operations after staffing-trigger events fell from a peak of 81 on November 8, 2025, to one on November 16, 2025. Related limits on some general-aviation, VFR, commercial-space, and parachute operations also ended with the order.
source: Federal Aviation Administration, DOT and FAA Announce Termination of FAA Emergency Order, Return to Normal Operations

headline: FAA Command Center plan on November 15 still listed a Philadelphia TRACON Area C staffing trigger
fact: The FAA Air Traffic Control System Command Center operations plan issued November 15, 2026 (ADVZY 074) listed a staffing trigger at PHL Area C, the Newark approach sector, for 2330-0330 UTC, alongside a Jacksonville Center South Area staffing trigger. The same plan also listed weather-related ground-delay programs and several multi-week runway closures at large airports.
source: FAA ATCSCC Current Operations Plan Advisory, ADVZY 074, 11/15/2026

headline: Newark remains under a 36/36 hourly schedule cap into late 2027
fact: The June 23, 2026, Federal Register extension leaves Newark Liberty limited to 36 scheduled arrivals and 36 scheduled departures per hour from 6:00 a.m. to 10:59 p.m. Eastern Time from October 25, 2026, through October 30, 2027, because certified professional controller staffing in Philadelphia TRACON Area C remains below target.
source: Federal Register, Operating Limitations at Newark Liberty International Airport (2026-12589)

headline: Newark approach sector still on the FAA staffing-trigger list on November 15
fact: The November 15, 2026, FAA Command Center operations plan listed PHL Area C, which handles Newark airspace, as a staffing trigger later that night. That is a same-day operational constraint, not a new published cap.
source: FAA ATCSCC Current Operations Plan Advisory, ADVZY 074, 11/15/2026

headline: Delta said it would add Hawaii flying from JFK in the winter 2026-27 program
fact: In a February 13, 2026, News Hub release, Delta said its largest seasonal Hawaii schedule would include added flying from Atlanta, Detroit, and New York JFK, alongside the return of Boston-Honolulu and a new Minneapolis-Maui route, beginning in the December 2026 holiday period.
source: Delta News Hub, Lei-ing down Delta's largest Hawaii schedule

headline: Delta will restore Boston-Honolulu nonstops on December 19, 2026
fact: Delta announced on February 13, 2026, that Boston-Honolulu nonstop service will return on December 19, 2026, operating daily in peak late-December travel and then four times weekly through the winter season on Airbus A330-300 aircraft.
source: Delta News Hub, Lei-ing down Delta's largest Hawaii schedule

headline: Honolulu regains a Boston nonstop as part of Delta's winter Hawaii buildup
fact: The same Delta release says Boston-Honolulu returns December 19, 2026, with daily holiday frequency stepping down to four weekly flights for the rest of the winter, and that the airline is also adding Hawaii flying from Atlanta and New York JFK.
source: Delta News Hub, Lei-ing down Delta's largest Hawaii schedule

headline: Delta planned added Atlanta-Hawaii flying in the winter 2026-27 schedule
fact: Delta's February 13, 2026, Hawaii schedule announcement said the winter program would include added flying from Atlanta, as well as Detroit and New York JFK, beginning with the December 2026 holiday period. The release did not print a city-pair frequency table for the Atlanta additions.
source: Delta News Hub, Lei-ing down Delta's largest Hawaii schedule

headline: O'Hare August 2026 passengers rose 2.73%; year-to-date through August is up 5.62%
fact: Chicago Department of Aviation's August 2026 summary, dated October 19, 2026, reports O'Hare total passenger volume of 8,238,466 in August, up 2.73% from August 2025, and 59,569,807 for January-August 2026, up 5.62%. September 2026 official totals were not yet posted in the same file series when checked on November 15, 2026.
source: Chicago Department of Aviation, O'Hare Operations, Passengers, Cargo Summary by Class, as of August 2026

headline: Midway August 2026 passengers were up 0.82%; year-to-date through August is up 2.36%
fact: The companion Midway summary for August 2026 reports total passenger volume of 1,904,559, up 0.82% year over year, and 13,274,735 for January-August, up 2.36%. The printed total is used as reported; Midway's class split has previously shown unusual non-revenue swings, so the headline is the airport total.
source: Chicago Department of Aviation, Midway Operations, Passengers, Cargo Summary by Class, as of August 2026

headline: American will start Chicago O'Hare-Tokyo Narita nonstops on March 27, 2027
fact: American Airlines announced on July 1, 2026, that it will launch service between Chicago O'Hare and Tokyo Narita on March 27, 2027, described as the airline's 11th long-haul route from O'Hare, in partnership with Japan Airlines.
source: American Airlines Newsroom, A new chapter for Chicago: American to launch nonstop service to Tokyo

headline: American scheduled new Chicago-Kahului, Hawaii, service from December 17, 2026
fact: In a January 22, 2026, network release, American said it would add Chicago O'Hare-Kahului (Maui) service on a Boeing 787-8 beginning December 17, and also listed new year-round O'Hare flights to Allentown, Pennsylvania, and Columbia, South Carolina, from May 21, 2026.
source: American Airlines Newsroom, American enhances the nation's premier network with new routes from Chicago and Los Angeles

headline: FAA lists DFW Runway 18L/36R closed into May 2027
fact: The FAA Command Center operations plan for November 15, 2026, lists Dallas/Fort Worth Runway 18L/36R closed until May 15, 2027, 0400Z, in the system-impact reports section.
source: FAA ATCSCC Current Operations Plan Advisory, ADVZY 074, 11/15/2026

headline: Houston Airport System September traffic fell about 4% to 4.6 million passengers
fact: Houston First, citing Houston Airport System figures, reported on November 3, 2026, that system traffic (Bush Intercontinental and Hobby combined) fell 4% in September 2026 to 4.6 million passengers, with year-to-date traffic almost 45.5 million, down 2%. The same article says Bush Intercontinental handled about 3.5 million passengers, down about 4%, and Hobby just over 1 million, down 3.4%.
source: Houston First, September Air Traffic Drops by 4% Over Last Year

headline: Hobby has two runways listed closed into late 2026 and early 2027
fact: The November 15, 2026, FAA operations plan lists William P. Hobby Runway 04/22 closed until December 31, 2026, 0359Z, and Runway 13L/31R closed until January 9, 2027, 1300Z.
source: FAA ATCSCC Current Operations Plan Advisory, ADVZY 074, 11/15/2026

headline: LAX September 2026 passengers were 5,817,942, up 0.15%; year-to-date is down 1.29%
fact: Los Angeles World Airports' September 2026 traffic comparison reports 5,817,942 total passengers at LAX in September, up 0.15% from September 2025, and 54,735,592 year-to-date through September, down 1.29%.
source: Los Angeles World Airports, Traffic Comparison (TCOM) September 2026

headline: San Diego September passengers rose 11.9% to 2,300,711; trailing-12-month volume is up 8.3%
fact: San Diego International Airport's September 2026 air traffic report shows 2,300,711 passengers, up 11.9% year over year, with available seats up 16.5% and a 75.7% seat factor, down 3.4 points. Trailing-12-month passengers were 27,203,739, up 8.3%, and calendar year-to-date passengers were 20,629,598, up 10.0%.
source: San Diego County Regional Airport Authority, September 2026 Air Traffic Report

headline: Phoenix Sky Harbor September passengers fell 0.7% to 3,684,236; Q3 was down 0.90%
fact: The City of Phoenix Aviation Department's September 2026 monthly statistics report 3,684,236 passengers, down 0.7% from 3,710,694 in September 2025. Third-quarter 2026 passengers totaled 11,574,094, down 0.90%, and calendar year-to-date passengers through September were 38,226,978.
source: City of Phoenix Aviation Department, Monthly Statistics September 2026

headline: Spirit Airlines recorded no Phoenix passenger volume in September 2026
fact: Phoenix Sky Harbor's September 2026 monthly statistics show Spirit Airlines with no printed passengers, a 100% decline from 10,235 passengers in September 2025.
source: City of Phoenix Aviation Department, Monthly Statistics September 2026

headline: Harry Reid September passengers fell 8.43% to 4,076,634; year-to-date is down 7.29%
fact: The Clark County Department of Aviation's September 2026 passenger release reports 4,076,634 passengers at Harry Reid International, down 8.43% from 4,451,690 in September 2025. Year-to-date passengers were 38,429,929, down 7.29%. Domestic traffic was down 9.2% and international traffic was up 5.9%. Southwest carried 1,707,930 passengers, down 4%, while Frontier carried 417,690, up 39.5%. Spirit volume is deplaned and estimated in the release.
source: Clark County Department of Aviation, September 2026 Passenger Statistics press release

headline: SFO September passengers rose 5.1% to 4,654,309; year-to-date is up 2.5%
fact: San Francisco International Airport's September 2026 air traffic summary reports 4,654,309 passengers, up 5.1% from September 2025, and 41,875,194 calendar year-to-date through September, up 2.5%.
source: San Francisco International Airport, September 2026 and CYTD Air Traffic Summary

headline: Sea-Tac January-September 2026 passengers were 40,411,413, down 0.1%
fact: The Port of Seattle's third-quarter 2026 performance report shows Seattle-Tacoma International Airport handled 40,411,413 passengers in the first nine months of 2026, compared with 40,457,057 in the same period of 2025, a 0.1% decline. Domestic traffic was down 0.7% and international traffic was up 3.9%.
source: Port of Seattle, Q3 2026 Performance Report

headline: FAA listed Sea-Tac Runway 16C/34C closed through November 15, 2026
fact: The November 15, 2026, FAA Command Center operations plan lists Seattle-Tacoma Runway 16C/34C closed until November 15, 2026, 2359Z. That closure may already have expired later the same calendar day.
source: FAA ATCSCC Current Operations Plan Advisory, ADVZY 074, 11/15/2026

headline: Miami September passengers fell 1.82% to 3,573,815; year-to-date is down 1.20%
fact: Miami-Dade Aviation Department's September 2026 traffic report shows 3,573,815 total passengers, down 1.82% from September 2025. International passengers rose 1.28% to 1,647,207, while domestic passengers fell 4.33% to 1,926,608. Calendar year-to-date passengers were 41,041,584, down 1.20%.
source: Miami-Dade Aviation Department, September 2026 Traffic Report

headline: Orlando August passengers fell 6.89% to 4,375,567; trailing-12-month volume is still up 1.68%
fact: Greater Orlando Aviation Authority's August 2026 traffic summary reports 4,375,567 passengers, down 6.89% from August 2025, with calendar year-to-date passengers of 38,961,312, up 0.04%, and a last-12-month total of 57,687,961, up 1.68%. An official September 2026 traffic PDF was not retrievable when checked (the expected September file returned 403).
source: Greater Orlando Aviation Authority, Traffic Report August 2026

headline: Orlando's October 2026 average daily schedule is 518 departures and 93,399 seats
fact: GOAA's October 2026 average daily departures addendum, published in mid-September, shows 518 daily departures, up 1.9%, and 93,399 daily seats, up 2.2%. Frontier is listed at 59 daily departures, up 44.1%, with seats up 51.7%; Breeze departures are up 53.8%; and Southwest is listed at 166 daily departures, up 12.1%.
source: Greater Orlando Aviation Authority, October 2026 Average Daily Departures

headline: FAA lists Orlando Runway 17L/35R closed through November 20, 2026
fact: The November 15, 2026, FAA Command Center operations plan lists Orlando International Runway 17L/35R closed until November 20, 2026, 2100Z.
source: FAA ATCSCC Current Operations Plan Advisory, ADVZY 074, 11/15/2026

headline: Dulles last-12-month passengers through May 2026 were 28,752,936, up 1.49%
fact: The Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority May 2026 Air Traffic Statistics report, posted in July, shows Dulles International last-12-month passengers of 28,752,936, compared with 28,331,066 a year earlier, up 1.49%. Later monthly PDFs for June-September 2026 were not found at predictable MWAA file paths when checked on November 15, 2026.
source: Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority, May 2026 Air Traffic Statistics

headline: FAA lists Dulles Runway 01C/19C closed through November 22, 2026
fact: The November 15, 2026, FAA Command Center operations plan lists Washington Dulles Runway 01C/19C closed until November 22, 2026, 2359Z.
source: FAA ATCSCC Current Operations Plan Advisory, ADVZY 074, 11/15/2026

headline: FAA lists Nashville Runway 13/31 closed through January 1, 2027
fact: The November 15, 2026, FAA Command Center operations plan lists Nashville International Runway 13/31 closed until January 1, 2027, 2359Z.
source: FAA ATCSCC Current Operations Plan Advisory, ADVZY 074, 11/15/2026
